packageRules.description: boto3 and botocore release together, and an exact pin of one needs the matching other, so update them in one PR instead of two that must be merged in order (INFRA-614).

The Vercel AI SDK packages (ai and its @ai-sdk/* providers) release together from one monorepo, so update them in one PR per repository instead of one per package (INFRA-999). Major updates still come in a separate PR from minor and patch ones.
The @letsmod/dcl-* packages are released together from the dcl-kit monorepo with one shared version, so update them in one PR per repository instead of one per package (INFRA-808).

Bump the package.json range of our own npm packages on every release, even one the current range already allows, so the manifest states the minimum version a repository needs (INFRA-808). Offer the jump from 0.x to CalVer (2026.MDD.N): Renovate skips a major increment above 500 by default, to catch accidental date-based versions (INFRA-991).

Our own npm packages (dcl-kit, pimcore-link) have only our repositories as consumers, so run their updates at any time instead of waiting for the weekend, and open them ahead of other updates when PR limits apply, so a release reaches its consumers within hours (INFRA-965).

Repositories pin exact ci-pipelines release tags and adopt each release through this update, so run it at any time instead of waiting for the weekend, and open it ahead of other updates when PR limits apply (INFRA-959).

Offer Python patch updates on their own branch, so holding a new minor version for approval (next rule) doesn't hold back patch releases. Must not match on update type: Renovate decides the split before the update type is known.

A new Python minor version often lands before the libraries and tools a repository depends on support it, so hold it on the Dependency Dashboard until someone approves it there. Patch updates are not affected.
